why: The three trouble lanes (raise/clear/reconcile) each write one emission file and rely on TroubleShim.drain() to fold it. drain() has exactly two callers: receive_raise (the in-process poke, which needs _trouble_notifier wired in the SAME process) and on_pulse (the shim's beat). MEASURED 2026-09-08: `systemctl --user list-units 'cairn*'` lists two units, cairn-ground-loop and cairn-web-server; pgrep shows those two processes and nothing else. No process hosts the trouble shim, so on_pulse never fires, so the beat backstop the lane's docstrings promise ('the emission is on disk either way, and the beat drains it') does not exist. Emissions pile up until a hand runs the drain. Measured effect today: a hand-run drain folded 39 emissions spanning 22:41 to 00:48 UTC, including a reconcile that cleared 23 stale inspector findings which had been sitting in the operator inbox. The ground loop pulses PROBES (cairn/devices/<d>/probes/*.py), not shims, and a probe that drained would be a probe with authority — so this is not fixed by adding a probe, and not by a daemon (that reflex is drift). It wants the rack, which is the next rung of the ruled ladder and is not built.
